title: Keyboard Manager ceases functionality when using Anywhere PCoIP remote software

status.label: Confirm the PCoIP failure on current stable
status.detail: The report says PowerToys 0.92.1 key swaps fail over Anywhere PCoIP and can leave Ctrl/Alt unusable until Keyboard Manager is turned off, while local input works.

judgment.rationale: The reporter lists PowerToys 0.92.1, Windows 11 build 26100.6584, and Anywhere PCoIP client 25.06.03. Swapping Ctrl, Alt, and Windows keys works locally but reportedly fails over PCoIP, sometimes leaving Ctrl and Alt unusable until Keyboard Manager is disabled. The report says the behavior occurs whether PowerToys is on the host or remote machine and that the PCoIP vendor directed the reporter to PowerToys. There are no comments, so a current-version confirmation is the next discriminating evidence before selecting an input-hook investigation.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.92.1 from the Microsoft Store and Windows 11 build 26100.6584.
The reported remote software is Anywhere PCoIP client 25.06.03, built by HP.
The reporter swaps Ctrl, Alt, and Windows keys; the remaps work locally but fail during PCoIP sessions.
Ctrl and Alt reportedly stop working entirely until Keyboard Manager is turned off.
The reporter says the problem occurs when PowerToys is installed on either the host or remote machine.
The issue has no comments or assignees.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the failure still occurs on current stable with PCoIP and whether disabling Keyboard Manager restores Ctrl and Alt.

fix_assessment.rationale: The only report is from PowerToys 0.92.1, and no current-version result or input trace confirms a live Keyboard Manager defect. The remote-client interaction should be retested before proposing a code fix.

issue_context.analysis: The report distinguishes remote PCoIP input from local keyboard use and describes a serious modifier failure, but it uses an older PowerToys build. Confirm the behavior on current stable and retain the host-versus-remote setup detail before deciding whether to trace an input-hook interaction.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body, labels, and discussion; there are no comments or assignees.
Compared the reported PCoIP behavior with #42041's separate remote-control key-state report; the remote clients and mapped keys differ, so no duplicate or shared fix is established.

information_gaps.information: Whether the Ctrl/Alt remap failure and stuck-modifier behavior persist on current stable with Anywhere PCoIP 25.06.03, and whether disabling Keyboard Manager restores the keys
information_gaps.why_needed: The report lists PowerToys 0.92.1; a current retest determines whether an active PowerToys defect remains.

comment.body: Thanks for specifying Anywhere PCoIP 25.06.03, Windows 11 build 26100.6584, and that the remaps work locally but Ctrl/Alt can stop working remotely. Since the report lists PowerToys 0.92.1, could you confirm whether this still happens on current stable and whether turning off Keyboard Manager restores Ctrl and Alt?
